current_date: Document and page titled 'Tyneside Validation Checklist 2024' (file name says 'Jan 25'); no explicit adoption date in the text
current_evidence: The Newcastle 'Validation of planning applications in Tyneside' page links this PDF as the checklist and says 'This latest document supersedes the validation checklist published in 2019'. Neither the page nor a search mentions a newer version. A 'Revised Tyneside Validation Checklist 2024 - Your Chance to Comment' consultation page exists, but it could not be opened because the fetch budget ran out.

issues.detail: Grokbot also used Gateshead's superseded 2019 'Tyne and Wear validation list' as a source, mixing it with the current list: 14 of 31 tab_items and 6 app_type_rows come from it. Examples are the Householder 'Minerals / Waste specific statements' row, Cycle parking, Travel Plan, Block plan, Heritage Statement ('see requirement 16'; in the current list Heritage Statement is note 19) and the Full planning Ecological Survey row.
issues.evidence: Validation page: 'This latest document supersedes the validation checklist published in 2019.' Grokbot source: gateshead.gov.uk/media/6692/Tyne-and-Wear-validation-list-2019/...

issues.detail: Many tab_items are duplicates. 'For any supporting documents, we prefer these with signatures already redacted or provided in a typed form' appears 9 times, with page or checklist fragments attached ('98 Checklist 2:', '23 15.', '60 Checklist 2:'). The location plan scale, site plan, plan numbering, furniture layout and HRA items each appear twice: once from the current page/PDF and once from the 2019 Gateshead list.

About 20 of the 31 tab_items are boilerplate, process or reference text, not requirements. They include the page title/navigation ('Validation of planning applications in Tyneside | Newcastle City Council ... Have your say'), the links disclaimer and data protection text, 'paper copies ... not recommended', the redaction instructions, 'Failure to submit the required information will result in your application being made invalid', policy reference lists ('Newcastle and Gateshead Core Strategy Policies CS1, CS13...'), and broken link fragments ('445.pdf', 'anuary%202020.pdf'). The app_type_rows 'Employment / Economic Statement' and 'Pre-application advice' are not requirements either: the first quotes text saying the statement is not needed for validation, and the second is contents-list text.
issues.evidence: 'Applicants can also submit an Economic Statement ... but this would not be required for validation purposes.'; 'the Checklists Pre-Application Advice Local Authority Contact Details Appendix 1...'

issues.detail: Two Householder rows contradict the source. 'Coal Mining / Land Stability Risk Assessment' and the 2019-sourced 'Minerals / Waste specific statements' are listed for Householder, but their own trigger text exempts householder extensions and alterations.
issues.evidence: Note 15: 'A coal mining risk assessment is normally only required for development in Coal Mining Development High Risk Areas with the exception of householder extensions or alterations, changes of use and shop front alterations'.

issues.detail: Under 'Change of use - prior approval', Grokbot lists Block/Site plan, Design Code/Masterplan and Landscaping scheme, although the quoted triggers exclude change of use. The site plan trigger excludes change of use only. The landscape strategy/masterplan covers major applications 'other than wholly change of use/conversion applications'. Landscaping Details (note 23) covers planning applications 'except those for the change of use or alteration to an existing building'. Structural Survey (barn conversions) is a planning application requirement, not a prior approval one.
issues.evidence: Note 22: 'All major planning applications ... other than wholly change of use/conversion applications'; Note 23: 'Planning applications (except those for the change of use or alteration to an existing building)'.

issues.detail: The current list has 8 checklists by application type: Full; Outline & Reserved Matters; LBC & Relevant Demolition in a Conservation Area; Advertisement; Householder; Non-material/Minor-material Amendments; Lawful Development Certificate; and Prior Approval. Despite this, Grokbot places 48 rows under Full planning as 'INFERRED' (e.g. Telecommunications, Schedule of works (listed building), Advertisement drawings). It marks Reserved matters, Advertisement, Lawful development cert, Demolition in conservation area and Non-material amendment as '(none)'. Reserved matters is contradicted by Grokbot's own Sustainability Statement excerpt ('Major full planning applications and major reserved matter applications'). Demolition in a conservation area triggers a Heritage Statement and Marketing Information. Outline lists only a Travel Plan.
issues.evidence: Appendix 2 checklist list; Note 24 Marketing: 'Demolition of listed and locally listed buildings, and buildings in conservation areas'.

issues.detail: Several triggers come from the wrong requirement. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' and 'Construction (Environmental) Management Plan' both use a SuDS Construction Method Statement sentence. 'Noise Impact Assessment' uses kitchen-extraction text, while the real Acoustic and Vibration trigger was put on the 'Odour / Dust / Vibration' row. 'Planning Statement' uses affordable-housing guidance text. 'Planning Obligations' uses BNG-specific S106 text. 'Block plan / Site plan' uses the national-requirements contents list from the 2019 Gateshead list.
issues.evidence: Grokbot Schedule of works trigger: 'A Construction Method Statement for the proposed SuDS including construction processes to protect the SuDS functionality...'

issues.detail: Many triggers are fragments or content-format rules, not statements of when the item applies. Examples: Design and Access Statement 'Design and Access Statement (if required) 8.'; Archaeology 'Archaeological desk based assessment'; Arboricultural 'development an Arboricultural Impact Assessment will be required (see section 35).'; Marketing 'conservation areas Marketing information will not always be required.'; Minerals 'sterilisation of mineral resources.'; Tall buildings 'near other tall buildings.'; Drainage 'strategies and SuDS design and promote consistency...'; Fire Statement is just the guidance link. Contaminated Land, Foul Sewage, Affordable Housing, Housing mix, Ventilation and Sequential Test all quote 'The title must state the document is/includes...'. The source triggers include: Housing space standards for 'All applications for new homes' (plus M4(2) for 25% of new-build schemes of 10+ dwellings in Newcastle); Land Contamination for 'All new development with a sensitive end use' and land on the contaminated register; Heritage Statement for LBC, major applications in or affecting conservation areas, and any application affecting a heritage asset.

The Health Impact Assessment excerpt quotes the Gateshead wording ('In Gateshead, HIA will be required for...'). The Newcastle wording is 'likely to be required for (but not limited to)': major residential applications of more than 100 units and employment sites of 10 ha or more. The excerpt also starts mid-list ('Employment sites of 10 hectares or more In Gateshead...').
issues.evidence: Note 18: Newcastle: 'Health Impact Assessments (HIA) are likely to be required for (but not limited to):'

issues.detail: Local note 26 'Overheating Assessment and Mitigation Requirements' is not captured anywhere; its trigger text was not read because the fetch budget ran out. Landscaping Details (note 23: planning applications except change of use or alteration to an existing building, where landscaping is significant) is missing from Full planning and Householder, and appears only under prior approval, where it does not apply. The simple contamination screening for single dwellings on previously undeveloped land (Newcastle, Gateshead and South Tyneside) is not captured.
issues.evidence: Appendix 1 heading list: '26. Overheating Assessment and Mitigation Requirements'; Note 21: 'applications for single dwellings on land identified as previously undeveloped land' require a simple screening assessment.

issues.detail: The List date 2025-01-01 comes from PDF metadata. The document and web page call it 'Tyneside Validation Checklist 2024', and only the file name says 'Jan 25'. No adoption date appears in the text, so the date should be recorded with that basis, not as metadata.
Grokbot does not mention the council's online validation tool, which the validation page links alongside the PDF. Users may be directed to it for some application types.
issues.evidence: Validation page link: 'Welcome to the Newcastle City Council Validation Check Service. - PlanX' (planningservices.newcastle.gov.uk/validation-requirements-live), noted as 'still in development'.

summary: Grokbot's link is the current joint Tyneside Validation Checklist (titled 2024, file dated Jan 25). The extraction mixes in the superseded 2019 Gateshead list, is full of boilerplate and duplicate items, and has many wrong or fragmentary triggers and inverted application-type placements, such as the householder coal-mining item and change-of-use items the source excludes. Notes 25-39 were checked only by heading because the fetch budget ran out.
